The Antonelli you don't know: Inside the Mercedes garage with F1's new world champion

DM
By David Miller Formula 1 & Motorsport Telemetry Specialist • via Autosport Wire
⚡ Visual Story
Source & Photography: Autosport Wire Dispatch Verified Editorial Asset
⚡ Executive Takeaways & Key Highlights
  • Mercedes mechanics have learned to watch their backs.
  • Not because of the dangers of a pitstop, but because of Kimi Antonelli .
  • Formula 1's newly crowned world champion has a rather unusual habit.
⚡ EDITORIAL TAKE • DAVID MILLER Formula 1 & Motorsport Telemetry Specialist

Aerodynamic Efficiency & Motorsport Racecraft

In premier motorsport disciplines, millisecond gains represent months of high-intensity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) research. The developments reported by Autosport underline how tire degradation curves, ground-effect aero seals, and power-unit energy recovery systems dictate race outcomes. Technical compliance under strict cost caps continues to test team engineering depth.

Big Picture: Upcoming grand prix telemetry and trackside upgrades will reveal which teams hold the definitive technical advantage.

Mercedes mechanics have learned to watch their backs. Not because of the dangers of a pitstop, but because of Kimi Antonelli . Formula 1's newly crowned world champion has a rather unusual habit. He approaches members of his crew, greets them and, when they least expect it, gives their nipples a pinch - so nobody appears to be safe!

📌 The Core Development

It is just one of the many practical jokes through which the 20-year-old Italian has developed a special relationship with the people who work on his W17. But behind the mischief, seemingly so far removed from the image of a world champion, lies something much more significant.

Success has roots that are not always visible. To understand them, you sometimes have to look beyond what happens on the track. In Antonelli's case, that means listening to the people who share the work, pressure and emotions of a grand prix weekend with him.

🔍 Background & Sector Context

Their accounts paint a picture of a young man who has earned something that even a world championship cannot guarantee: the trust and respect of those around him. It is a relationship that developed naturally, rooted in an attitude Antonelli learned long before reaching F1, when he accompanied his father Marco to races with his own team. Growing up around workshops and racing circuits taught him a valuable lesson: before becoming a racing driver, you have to learn how to be part of a team.

"When he comes into the garage, it's quite a show," said Nathan Tupper, who works on the power unit of Antonelli's car. "He grabs everyone, pinches people's nipples, slaps them all over and generally causes chaos. At the end of the day, he's 20 years old. That's just Kimi."

📊 Industry & Real-World Impact

Ash Jones, the second senior mechanic on Antonelli's car, agrees: "There are so many practical jokes that it would be difficult to list them all. He comes over, says hello and then gives you a pinch. That's how he jokes around with us. He likes having a good relationship with everyone, laughing and having fun together."

🔮 Strategic Outlook & What Lies Ahead

The jokes do not even stop when the circumstances would seem to demand maximum concentration. Tom Mason, Antonelli's number one mechanic, has seen it countless times: "It always makes me laugh watching him getting ready to get into the car before qualifying. He's still joking around, grabbing the guys, tickling them. Even when the pressure is enormous, he's there having fun. He's incredibly relaxed."

The driver who has displayed such remarkable maturity on the track is the same young man who, the moment he walks into the garage, becomes a 20-year-old eager to have some fun. Birthdays are another occasion for the Mercedes mechanics to be on their guard, as Antonelli has introduced a tradition of celebrating his colleagues by covering their faces in whipped cream.
